intro: Picture waking up in the morning, stepping out of your room, and finding a wide private lake with a cable strung across it for towing wakeboards — Atlantis Extreme Park is a small activity-focused resort in Khok Mai Lai sub-district, on the outskirts of Prachinburi toward Khao Yai / Na Di, that combines a place to stay with a wakeboarding park (Wake Park) all in one spot · besides swimming and kayaking on the lake, it also has a Thai herbal sauna, a massage room, an outdoor Muay Thai gym and ring, and a restaurant serving Spanish, Italian, and Western dishes · it's a specialized stay for people who want an active holiday rather than a polished luxury resort · there aren't many rooms and they book up fairly fast, with rates starting around THB 900/night · just so you know, online reviews are still very limited, so the scores you see come from a small sample and are better read as a guide than as fixed numbers

body.html: Who Atlantis Extreme Park is right for — to put it as simply as possible, this isn't a resort you come to just to lie around; it's an activity-focused stay with a wakeboarding park built in · the core concept of Atlantis Extreme Park is to place the accommodation right beside a private lake fitted with a cable system for towing wakeboards, then add other activities like kayaking, swimming, an outdoor Muay Thai gym, a herbal sauna, and a massage room · so the people it suits best are groups of friends who like adrenaline activities, active couples, and families who want their kids to get outside and play instead of staring at a screen · both beginner and experienced wakeboarders can come here, because the cable system works well for learning from the very start · on the flip side, if you're looking for a luxury resort with a beautiful lobby, spotless rooms in every corner, a full-service spa, and five-star service, this may not be the answer, because Atlantis positions itself as a small specialized stay that sells experience rather than luxury · another group that fits well is people using Prachinburi as a base to explore Khao Yai and Nakhon Nayok Waterfall who want a place with something to do in the evening after getting back, rather than just sitting in the room

Location and getting there — Atlantis Extreme Park sits on Suwannason Road in Khok Mai Lai sub-district, Mueang Prachinburi district, which is the outskirts stretching toward Khao Yai and Na Di district · the nearest landmark is Nong Cha-om fruit market, a well-known spot in this area · it's about 15 km from Prachinburi town, roughly a 15-20 minute drive · the clearest advantage of this location is how close it is to nature — it's only about a 15-20 minute drive to Nakhon Nayok Waterfall and the route up to Khao Yai National Park on this side, which makes it easy to use as a base for day trips · people driving from Bangkok usually come via Route 305 (Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok) or the motorway and then on into Prachinburi, taking about 2-2.5 hours depending on your starting point and traffic · to be honest, this is an out-of-town stay built around arriving by private car and isn't well suited to relying on public transport, because the surroundings are semi-rural and shops and convenience stores aren't right at the gate · the upside is that there's free parking on site, and the surroundings are quiet and shaded by trees, good for getting away from the bustle of the city

"Came to wakeboard with friends and stayed the night. So much fun, the grounds are spacious, the lake is beautiful, and in the evening we went for a herbal sauna. It felt like escaping out into nature, and it's close to Khao Yai too. Well worth it for a weekend trip."

Room types and decor — the first thing to understand is that Atlantis Extreme Park is a very small place to stay · information from booking platforms lists only around 5-7 rooms/suites, which means that during long weekends or Saturdays and Sundays when lots of people come to wakeboard, rooms fill up fast and you should book ahead · the rooms are simple but fully functional, all with air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with cable channels, a refrigerator, a kettle, a desk, and a private bathroom with a shower and basic toiletries · what many people like is that most rooms are lake-view rooms that open onto water and trees, which feels relaxing and gives you the full sense of being out in nature · since this is an activity-focused stay, the rooms aren't decorated in a luxe boutique style but emphasize cleanliness and convenience for people who spend most of their time outside rather than in the room · something for families to know: the booking system notes that extra beds and cribs are not available in any room type, so if you're coming with several people or bringing young children, ask the resort directly about the number of guests per room and the room setup before booking, so there are no surprises at check-in

Facilities, the lake, and activities — this is the heart of Atlantis Extreme Park and the main reason people choose to come here · the number-one highlight is the private lake fitted with a cable system for towing wakeboards (Wake Park), which lets you wakeboard without needing a tow boat — this system works really well for learning from a beginner level, because the speed is steady and controllable · besides wakeboarding, you can also kayak and swim in the same lake · on land there's an outdoor Muay Thai gym and ring among the trees for anyone who wants to work out or try a bit of boxing · on the relaxation side there's a Thai herbal steam sauna and a Thai aroma massage room to ease tired muscles after a full day of activities · there's a fitness room, barbecue service, a bar, free Wi-Fi, and free parking · another thing many people ask about is pets — information from booking platforms notes that pets are allowed to stay at no extra charge, which is rare for ordinary accommodation, so it's a plus for anyone who wants to bring their dog or cat along · one thing to be aware of is that, since this is a small resort, the shared facilities focus mainly on outdoor activities; there's no resort-style swimming pool or luxurious common areas, and some services may need to be arranged in advance or carry a separate charge, such as wakeboarding fees or equipment rental, so check clearly before you go

Food and bar — what sets Atlantis Extreme Park apart from the typical out-of-town stay is the food · the resort restaurant serves a fairly distinctive menu, including Spanish dishes (such as paella, Spanish omelette, churros), Italian dishes (spaghetti, pizza, risotto), and Western food (American breakfast, burgers, fries) · several real reviews speak positively about the Western food here, saying it tastes good and is done more seriously than you'd expect for a small place outside town · there's barbecue service for groups who want to grill their own food by the lake, and a bar for sipping a drink in the evening · one thing to plan ahead for is that the room rate does not include breakfast, so if you want a morning meal you should order from the resort restaurant or have a plan ready · and because it's a small restaurant at a small property, some menu items may need to be ordered in advance or be limited at certain times, so it's a good idea to ask the resort about the menu and the kitchen's opening hours beforehand, especially if you're coming as a large group or during the off-season

Service — because this is a small property run by just a few staff, the service at Atlantis Extreme Park feels friendly, more like a family-run resort than a hotel with rigid systems · the real reviews that do exist speak positively about the owner and the team, saying they're attentive, happy to advise on activities and wakeboarding, and willing to help arrange meals · the upside of a small place is that you usually get to talk to the person who can actually make decisions, which makes it easy to tweak this or that · but on the other hand, being a small property also means that some services aren't available around the clock the way they would be at a big hotel, and when it's busy the team may have to handle several things at once · the trick is to communicate ahead — calling or messaging the resort in advance about check-in time, the activities you want to do, and meals will make everything run more smoothly than waiting until you arrive to ask

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — to be upfront, Atlantis Extreme Park is a specialized stay with very few online reviews compared with ordinary hotels · on platforms like Trip.com the score shown reaches as high as a perfect 10, but it comes from a very small sample, while some platforms have no reviews at all, so these numbers are better read as a guide than treated as a benchmark · on the praise side: the points people agree on are the spacious, shaded grounds, good for escaping the city to be in nature; the fun of wakeboarding and kayaking on the lake, which is hard to find anywhere else in this area; the herbal sauna and massage room that help you unwind after a full day; the surprisingly tasty Western food; and how well it suits coming as a group of friends, a couple, or a family · many people conclude it's a great fit for a weekend trip · on the gripe side: because it's a small place, there are few rooms and they're hard to book at peak times; the shared facilities are limited compared with a big resort; there's no breakfast included in the rate; it's out of town so you need a private car; and it's an activity-focused stay that may not suit you if you want everything polished and luxurious in every corner · overall these gripes are more about setting your expectations to match the concept than they are quality problems

"Brought the family while we were visiting Khao Yai, and the kids had a blast swimming and kayaking. The grounds are spacious enough to let them run around, and the Western food is tasty · the only downside is that there are few rooms so you have to book ahead, and there's no breakfast so you order your own, but overall we were impressed."

Price comparison and value — room rates at Atlantis Extreme Park run roughly THB 900-1,200/night for a standard room, and can rise during long weekends or Saturdays and Sundays when lots of people come to wakeboard (platform prices fluctuate by date and promotion, so check the actual dates before deciding) · if you look purely at the room rate compared with typical resorts in Prachinburi, it sits in the mid-range, neither the cheapest nor expensive · but what makes it good value is the built-in activities — for people who come specifically to wakeboard, kayak, and use the sauna, staying right next to the activity area saves both time and the cost of traveling back and forth, compared with staying elsewhere and driving over to play · on the flip side, if you're not interested in these activities and just want a clean room on a budget, there may be options in Prachinburi that give you better value for the same price · in short, the value here is tied to using the activities — the more you play, the more worthwhile the price becomes

Good to know before booking — there are several things that help make the trip go smoothly · one, because there are very few rooms (around 5-7), book ahead, especially for long weekends and Saturdays and Sundays, and confirm the number of guests per room clearly, since the system notes that extra beds aren't available · two, ask clearly about wakeboarding fees and equipment rental — whether they're included in the room rate or charged separately, along with the hours it's open for play each day · three, this place has no included breakfast, so plan your morning meal ahead, whether ordering from the resort restaurant or stopping to buy something on the way · four, it's an out-of-town stay so you should have a private car, and fill up on fuel and buy any essentials from town or a convenience store before heading in · five, if you're going to bring a pet, even though the information says it's allowed, you should give advance notice to keep things in order · six, because online reviews are still scarce, it's a good idea to contact the resort directly (for example via the Atlantis Wake Park Facebook page) to confirm that it's open, the current prices, and the activities available during the period you'll be visiting

Summary — based on the available information and real reviews, Atlantis Extreme Park is the best fit for people who want an active holiday, especially the wakeboarding and outdoor-activity crowd, in a location that easily works as a base for Khao Yai and Nakhon Nayok Waterfall · the built-in wakeboarding lake, the herbal sauna, the Muay Thai gym, the well-done Western food, and the pet-friendly policy give it a distinctive charm that's hard to find at the typical out-of-town stay · but you have to accept that this is a small resort with few rooms, thin online reviews, limited shared facilities, and no breakfast — it suits people coming for the experience rather than the luxury · if you're after the quiet of a foothill resort or a polished luxury stay, you may want to look at other options around Noen Hom or toward Khao Yai · but if you want a weekend trip where you can wake up and wakeboard right outside your room, with activities and a setting out in nature — Atlantis Extreme Park is a specialized option that fits this group spot-on, and it's a good idea to contact the resort directly to confirm the details before every trip

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Atlantis Extreme Park Prachinburi

faq.q: Where in Prachinburi is Atlantis Extreme Park · what's nearby?
faq.a: It's located at 198/10 Moo 7, Suwannason Road, Khok Mai Lai Sub-district, Mueang Prachinburi District, on the outskirts toward Khao Yai / Na Di · the nearest landmark is Nong Cha-om fruit market · it's about 15 km from Prachinburi town (15-20 min drive), and about a 15-20 minute drive to Nakhon Nayok Waterfall or the route up to Khao Yai National Park, so it works easily as a base for exploring nature

faq.q: Can you really wakeboard at Atlantis Extreme Park · what activities are there?
faq.a: Yes · the highlight is a private lake with a cable system for towing wakeboards (Wake Park), suitable for both beginners and experienced riders without needing a tow boat · in the same lake you can also kayak and swim · on land there's an outdoor Muay Thai gym and ring, a herbal sauna, and a massage room · it's a good idea to ask the resort about wakeboarding fees, equipment rental, and the hours it's open for play, since they may be charged separately from the room rate

faq.q: What's the starting price at Atlantis Extreme Park · what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start around THB 900-1,200/night for a standard lake-view room, rising during long weekends or Saturdays and Sundays · this is a small resort with only around 5-7 rooms/suites, and the booking system notes that extra beds aren't available · platform prices fluctuate by date and promotion, so check the actual dates and compare several channels before booking

faq.q: Does Atlantis Extreme Park have breakfast and allow pets?
faq.a: Breakfast is not included in the room rate, but there's a resort restaurant serving Spanish, Italian, and Western dishes, plus barbecue service · as for pets, information from booking platforms notes that pets are allowed to stay at no extra charge, but you should give the resort advance notice to keep things in order

faq.q: Who is Atlantis Extreme Park right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for groups of friends, active couples, and families who like outdoor activities, especially people who want to wakeboard, kayak, and unwind with a herbal sauna, while using it as a base for Khao Yai and Nakhon Nayok Waterfall · if you're looking for a polished luxury resort, full shared facilities, or want breakfast at your stay, a foothill resort around Noen Hom may suit you better

faq.q: How do you book Atlantis Extreme Park reliably · are the reviews trustworthy?
faq.a: Because it's a small specialized stay, online reviews are still very scarce; the score on some platforms is high but comes from a small sample, so read it as a guide · the most reliable way is to contact the resort directly via the Atlantis Wake Park page to confirm it's open, room availability, current prices, and the activities on offer during the period you'll visit, before transferring money or confirming the booking
